issues: Privacy: the printed imprint gives an e-mail address and phone number. SpaceBook keeps only the board's website.

Pictures of a sunrise over mountains and a river, and of a sunset with sailing boats; a boy stands with arms spread facing the Sun, with North, East and South marked on the ground.
issues: The text explains sunrise and sunset by the Earth's revolution ("revolves around the Sun … from West to East"). In fact the daily rising and setting of the Sun is caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis from West to East; revolution causes the seasons. Kept as printed.

decorative: A picture of a house with a direction marker (North arrow up, East arrow right); a torch shining on a box casts a long shadow behind it.

issues: In Q2 the three pictures are not labelled. Picture 1 has the Sun at top-left with a shadow to the right; picture 2 has the Sun overhead with a short shadow; picture 3 has the Sun on the right (East, by the printed compass) with a long shadow to the left. SpaceBook reads them as evening, noon and morning; the order is a SpaceBook reading of the art.

decorative: Photos of an offshore oil rig, wind turbines on a hill and a waterfall in a forest; a doctor checking a patient's blood pressure, a carpenter at work and a farmer sowing seed in a field.
issues: The "Know That!" box says the Khewra salt mines are "the second largest". They are usually described as the second-largest salt mine in the world. Kept as printed.

issues: The activity list has 10 items, but the printed table has only five rows, numbered i, ii, iii, "vi", v ("vi" is a misprint for iv). Kept as printed.

issues: In the printed insect life-cycle picture the labels "Larva" and "Pupa" are swapped: the green chrysalis is labelled "Larva" and the caterpillar is labelled "Pupa". The SpaceBook diagram below labels them correctly (caterpillar = larva, chrysalis = pupa). Item iv says the pupa develops "into insects"; this means the adult insect. Kept as printed.

The "Do you know?" box says the Sun is "11990 times bigger than Earth". This is not correct: the Sun's diameter is about 109 times the Earth's, and its volume is about 1.3 million times the Earth's. Kept as printed.

issues: The "Do you know?" box misspells Mongolia as "Mangolia". Kept as printed.

decorative: Three underwater/lake illustrations: an ocean scene with a sea horse, a shark, fishes, starfish and crabs (placed above the "Fresh water" heading); a freshwater lake with reeds, lotus flowers, fish, a duck, a crab and a frog on a lily pad; and a sea scene with a stingray, sea turtle, jellyfish, lobster, fishes, starfish and seaweed.

issues: The text and picture place polar bears and penguins together. Polar bears live only in the Arctic (north) and wild penguins live mostly in Antarctica and the southern oceans, so they do not meet in nature. Kept as printed.

issues: "90% area of Antarctica is covered with snow" — about 98% of Antarctica is covered by ice. Kept as printed.

issues: A polar bear's skin is actually black; the white colour that hides it in the snow comes from its fur. The label "the colour of skin" means the colour of its fur coat. Kept as printed.
